answerNotes.CAR: A car carries people on roads. Its trunk holds luggage, while the passenger compartment holds the seats.
answerNotes.HOSE: A hose is a flexible tube. A nozzle shapes the flow at one end, while a tap controls its supply at the other.
answerNotes.SOAP: Soap helps remove dirt when used with water. Rinsing carries away the loosened dirt and remaining suds.
answerNotes.WHEEL: A wheel rotates around an axle. Its tire is an outer covering, not another name for the entire wheel.
answerNotes.WINDOW: A window admits light through glass. A screen is a mesh barrier that can keep insects out when the glass is open.
answerNotes.WATER: Water is the same liquid whether it is in a drinking glass, a garden hose, or a cooking pot. The container changes the scene, not the substance.
answerNotes.WAX: Wax can form a candle or a protective coating. A candle consumes it as fuel, while polishing leaves a thin layer on a surface.

answerNotes.ROUTE: A route is a planned course. Several roads or stops can be parts of a single route.
answerNotes.ROAD: A road is a route for vehicles. A sidewalk or footpath provides a different part of the journey for people on foot.
answerNotes.TOWN: A town is a community. Its square or town hall is only one place within the larger community.
answerNotes.FOLD: Folding brings one part of a sheet over another. A crease is the line left by pressing that fold.

answerNotes.BAG: A bag is a flexible carrying container. A pocket is generally a smaller compartment attached to clothing or another bag.
answerNotes.HANDLE: A handle is the part made for the hand to grip. Its shape depends on whether the object is carried, pulled, poured, or turned.
answerNotes.LID: A lid is a removable cover. On a cooking pot it helps contain heat and steam; on a jar it closes the opening.
answerNotes.BLANKET: A blanket is a covering used for warmth. A quilt usually has several layers held together with stitching.
answerNotes.CAR: A car carries people on roads. Its trunk holds luggage, while the passenger compartment holds the seats.
answerNotes.LOAD: A load is the material being carried. The wheelbarrow or cart is the vehicle supporting that load.

answerNotes.RUBBER: Rubber bends and springs back. That makes it useful for balls and tires as well as waterproof footwear.
answerNotes.WINDOW: A window admits light through glass. A screen is a mesh barrier that can keep insects out when the glass is open.

answerNotes.TABLE: A table provides a raised flat surface. Chairs are the separate furniture used to sit beside it.
answerNotes.CAR: A car carries people on roads. Its trunk holds luggage, while the passenger compartment holds the seats.
answerNotes.SHADE: Shade blocks direct sunlight. A shaded garden corner still receives some light; it is different from a completely dark room.
answerNotes.TREE: Trees have woody trunks and branches. Familiar garden trees may provide fruit, flowers, or shade, sometimes all three.
answerNotes.SANDWICH: A sandwich places a filling between pieces of bread. An open-faced version uses just one supporting slice.
answerNotes.WATER: Water is the same liquid whether it is in a drinking glass, a garden hose, or a cooking pot. The container changes the scene, not the substance.
answerNotes.BENCH: A bench normally seats more than one person. It can be used in a park, entryway, or bus shelter without changing that basic meaning.
answerNotes.ROAD: A road is a route for vehicles. A sidewalk or footpath provides a different part of the journey for people on foot.
